protocol.instrument_name: Authority – Supply of specified restricted substances by pharmacists – management of minor dermatological conditions
protocol.instrument_version: Dated: 28 August 2026 (Dr Kerry Chant, Chief Health Officer; Delegation Number PH380, PH381, PH427). Revokes the instrument entitled 'Authority – Supply of restricted substances by pharmacists signed 29 August 2025'.
protocol.effective_date: 2026-08-28 (instrument dated 28 August 2026; 'This authority commences on publication.' — publication date not printed; 'This authority is cancelled on 1 September 2027, unless earlier cancelled.')
protocol.legal_basis: Section 10 Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Act 1966; Clauses 53, 170 and 171 of the Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Regulation 2008. Issued by Dr Kerry Chant, Chief Health Officer, a duly appointed delegate of the Secretary, NSW Health, pursuant to clauses 53, 170, and 171 of the Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Regulation 2008 for the purpose of section 10 of the Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Act 1966.
protocol.supervision_model: Document's own terminology: an 'approved pharmacist' (holding general registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (NSW), employed or engaged in an 'approved pharmacy', having successfully completed Training Pathway 1 or Training Pathway 2, and — if Training Pathway two was completed — having provided NSW Health with their details via the expanded-services form) may supply to an applicable patient a restricted substance listed in clause 2 'otherwise than on prescription subject to the conditions in clause 3 of this instrument'.
protocol.scope_summary: NSW Health Authority instrument (legal authorisation, not a clinical practice standard) permitting an approved pharmacist to supply listed restricted substances otherwise than on prescription for four 'minor dermatological conditions' — impetigo, herpes zoster, acute exacerbation of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, and acute exacerbation of mild plaque psoriasis — subject to the conditions in clause 3 and indication-specific age bands (2-65 inclusive for atopic dermatitis; 18+ for herpes zoster; 2+ for impetigo; 18+ for psoriasis). Dose, quantity and treatment duration are governed by four separate NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards, which are not part of this document.

inclusion.text: For Acute exacerbation of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis: the patient 'is aged between 2 and 65 years old (inclusive).'
For Herpes zoster (Shingles): the patient 'is aged 18 years or older.'
For Impetigo: the patient 'is aged 2 years or older.'
For Acute exacerbation of mild plaque psoriasis: the patient 'is aged 18 years or older.'
'The pharmacist must only supply the restricted substance for the indication listed for the restricted substance in clause 2, and only in the formulation and strength indicated in clause 2.'
Supply quantity does not exceed the duration of treatment specified in the relevant Practice Standards, except in the circumstances described in clause 3(c) (smallest available manufacturer's pack).

'The pharmacist acts in accordance with the relevant Practice Standards, including in relation to any limitations on the supply of medicines indicated in clause 2 to a patient based on their age or other factor, and circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional.'
'The patient and pharmacist must both be physically present at the approved pharmacy premises, for consultation with the patient to occur prior to supply.'

The pharmacist is an 'approved pharmacist' — holds general registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (NSW); is employed or engaged in an 'approved pharmacy'; and has successfully completed Training Pathway 1 (Australasian College of Pharmaceutical Society of Australia / NSW education on Dermatological Conditions, AND any additional training module(s) approved by the Chief Health Officer and listed on the NSW Health website) OR Training Pathway 2 (Queensland University of Technology / James Cook University courses AND any additional approved training module(s)); if Training Pathway two was completed, has also provided NSW Health with their full name, contact details, pharmacist registration number, intended services and location of services via the expanded-services form.

Supply occurs at an 'approved pharmacy' — offers the authorised services when an approved pharmacist is present; maintains up-to-date service availability listings via Healthdirect Australia; and has a consulting room that is not used for any other purpose, fully enclosed with adequate privacy, adequate lighting, comfortable ambient temperature, ready access to a hand washing facility and/or medical grade hand sanitisation products, and sufficient floor area for the patient, an accompanying person and the pharmacist.

Supply is made in accordance with the 'relevant Practice Standards' — the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for management of impetigo (section 2(a)), herpes zoster (2(b)), acute exacerbations of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis (2(c)), or acute exacerbations of mild plaque psoriasis (2(d)), as approved by the Chief Health Officer and published on the NSW Health website.

exclusion.text: The condition is not one of the four 'Minor dermatological conditions' — 'Acute exacerbation of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis; Herpes zoster; Impetigo; Acute exacerbation of mild plaque psoriasis'.
Acute exacerbation of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis in a patient who is not 'aged between 2 and 65 years old (inclusive)' (i.e. under 2 years or over 65 years).
Herpes zoster (Shingles) in a patient who is under 18 years of age ('is aged 18 years or older').
Impetigo in a patient who is under 2 years of age ('is aged 2 years or older').
Acute exacerbation of mild plaque psoriasis in a patient who is under 18 years of age ('is aged 18 years or older').

The substance supplied is not the one listed in clause 2 for that indication, or is not in the formulation and strength indicated in clause 2 — 'The pharmacist must only supply the restricted substance for the indication listed for the restricted substance in clause 2, and only in the formulation and strength indicated in clause 2.'

The quantity supplied exceeds the duration of treatment specified in the relevant Practice Standards and the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack does not exceed the specified quantity (i.e. the clause 3(c) exception does not apply).
The patient and pharmacist are not both physically present at the approved pharmacy premises, or consultation with the patient did not occur prior to supply.

The pharmacist is not an 'approved pharmacist' (including not holding the required training pathway) or the premises are not an 'approved pharmacy' (including failure to meet the consulting room requirements).
An 'age or other factor' limitation on supply set by the relevant Practice Standards precludes supply to this patient (clause 3(d) incorporates those limitations into this instrument).

exclusion_exceptions.text: 'If the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack of the medicine exceeds the quantity specified in the relevant Practice Standards, the pharmacist may supply the medicine in the smallest available size.'

diagnosis_pathways.name: Supply of a restricted substance for a minor dermatological condition — ordered conditions (clause 3)

steps.description: Definitions (clause 5): 'Minor dermatological conditions' means the conditions included in each of the relevant Practice Standards, being: Acute exacerbation of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis; Herpes zoster; Impetigo; Acute exacerbation of mild plaque psoriasis. 'An 'applicable patient' means a patient who for: i. Acute exacerbation of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, is aged between 2 and 65 years old (inclusive). ii. Herpes zoster (Shingles), is aged 18 years or older. iii. Impetigo, is aged 2 years or older. iv. Acute exacerbation of mild plaque psoriasis, is aged 18 years or older.'

gates.criterion: Presentation is one of: acute exacerbation of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis; herpes zoster; impetigo; acute exacerbation of mild plaque psoriasis
Patient meets the age band for the presented indication (atopic dermatitis 2-65 inclusive; herpes zoster 18 years or older; impetigo 2 years or older; psoriasis 18 years or older)

steps.description: Clause 3(a): 'The pharmacist must only supply the restricted substance for the indication listed for the restricted substance in clause 2, and only in the formulation and strength indicated in clause 2.' Clause 2 lists, for management of impetigo: Mupirocin 2% ointment (excluding nasal ointment) or cream (topical), Dicloxacillin (oral), Flucloxacillin (oral), Cefalexin (oral); for herpes zoster: Valaciclovir (oral), Famciclovir (oral), Aciclovir (oral); for acute exacerbations of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis: Methylprednisolone aceponate 0.1% lotion, ointment or fatty ointment, Triamcinolone acetonide 0.02% ointment, Mometasone furoate 0.1% ointment, Betamethasone dipropionate 0.05% ointment, Betamethasone valerate 0.1% ointment, Desonide 0.05% lotion, Pimecrolimus 1% cream, Crisaborole 2% ointment; for acute exacerbations of mild plaque psoriasis: Methylprednisolone aceponate 0.1% cream, ointment or fatty ointment, Mometasone furoate 0.1% cream, hydrogel or ointment, Betamethasone dipropionate 0.05% cream or ointment, Calcipotriol + betamethasone dipropionate 50 + 500 mcg/g ointment or foam.

gates.criterion: Selected substance, formulation and strength match the clause 2 entry for the presented indication

steps.description: Clause 3(b) and 3(c): 'The pharmacist must not supply a medicine indicated in clause 2 in a quantity that exceeds the duration of treatment specified in the relevant Practice Standards except in the circumstances described in clause 3(c) of this instrument.' 'If the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack of the medicine exceeds the quantity specified in the relevant Practice Standards, the pharmacist may supply the medicine in the smallest available size.'

gates.criterion: Supply quantity does not exceed the duration of treatment specified in the relevant Practice Standards (unless the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack exceeds the specified quantity)

steps.description: Clause 3(d): 'The pharmacist acts in accordance with the relevant Practice Standards, including in relation to any limitations on the supply of medicines indicated in clause 2 to a patient based on their age or other factor, and circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional.'

gates.criterion: No age or other factor limitation precludes supply, and no referral circumstance applies under the relevant Practice Standards

steps.description: Clause 3(e): 'The patient and pharmacist must both be physically present at the approved pharmacy premises, for consultation with the patient to occur prior to supply.' Clause 3(f): the name of the pharmacist providing the consultation as shown in the AHPRA Register of Pharmacists must be displayed at or near the consultation room.

gates.criterion: Patient and pharmacist both physically present at the approved pharmacy premises and consultation occurs prior to supply

steps.description: Clause 3(g): 'Pharmacists must make a full clinical record of the consultation using secure digital software. Records must be stored securely for a minimum of seven (7) years or, in the case of health information collected while the patient was under the age of 18 years—until the patient has attained the age of 25 years, and must contain:' patient identification details; date of consultation; pharmacist name and Healthcare Provider Identifier - Individual; information relevant to the diagnosis or treatment; any clinical opinion reached; actions and management plan taken; particulars of any medication supplied (name, form, strength and quantity); notes on information or advice given; any consent given; and any referrals made. Clause 3(h): records must be provided to authorised NSW Health personnel for inspection upon request.

Clause 3(i): 'The pharmacist must seek the patient's consent to share a record of the consultation and any subsequent consultations (including adverse events) with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice, where the patient has one, following consent by the patient. If the patient consents to the disclosure, the record must be shared within a week following the consultation.'

gates.criterion: Patient consents to disclosure of the consultation record to their usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice

treatments.notes: Clause 2(a): 'Mupirocin 2% ointment (excluding nasal ointment) or cream (topical)' for management of impetigo. Applicable patient for impetigo: aged 2 years or older. Supply only in the formulation and strength indicated in clause 2 (clause 3(a)). Quantity/duration governed by the 'NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for management of impetigo' (separate document, not part of this PDF); clause 3(c) permits supply of the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack if that pack exceeds the specified quantity. Dose, frequency, quantity and duration are NOT printed in this instrument. No pregnancy or lactation caveat is printed in this document.

red_flags.trigger_text: '… circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional.' (clause 3(d), as specified in the relevant Practice Standards)
'… any limitations on the supply of medicines indicated in clause 2 to a patient based on their age or other factor …' (clause 3(d))

'Acute exacerbation of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, is aged between 2 and 65 years old (inclusive).' — a patient under 2 years or over 65 years with atopic dermatitis is not eligible for supply under this instrument.

'Acute exacerbation of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, is aged between 2 and 65 years old (inclusive).' — a patient over 65 years with atopic dermatitis is not eligible for supply under this instrument.
'Herpes zoster (Shingles), is aged 18 years or older.' — a patient under 18 years with herpes zoster is not eligible for supply under this instrument.
'Impetigo, is aged 2 years or older.' — a patient under 2 years with impetigo is not eligible for supply under this instrument.
'Acute exacerbation of mild plaque psoriasis, is aged 18 years or older.' — a patient under 18 years with mild plaque psoriasis is not eligible for supply under this instrument.

routine: circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional (clause 3(d) — circumstances as specified in the relevant Practice Standards for impetigo, herpes zoster, acute exacerbations of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, or acute exacerbations of mild plaque psoriasis)

review_followup.when: Within a week following the consultation, if the patient consents to the disclosure
review_followup.what: Share the record of the consultation and any subsequent consultations (including adverse events) with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice, where the patient has one (clause 3(i)).

review_followup.when: For a minimum of seven (7) years following the consultation; for health information collected while the patient was under the age of 18 years — until the patient has attained the age of 25 years
review_followup.what: Store the full clinical record of the consultation securely using secure digital software (clause 3(g), page 3); records must be provided to authorised NSW Health personnel for inspection upon request (clause 3(h), page 3).
'This authority is cancelled on 1 September 2027, unless earlier cancelled.' (clause 7 Cancellation) — the authorisation ceases on this date.

conditions: 'Pharmacists must provide clinical records of consultations upon request to authorised NSW Health personnel for inspection.' (clause 3(h), page 3)

'The pharmacist must seek the patient's consent to share a record of the consultation and any subsequent consultations (including adverse events) with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice, where the patient has one, following consent by the patient. If the patient consents to the disclosure, the record must be shared within a week following the consultation.' (clause 3(i), page 3)

Definitions, approved pharmacist (iii): 'if the pharmacist has completed Training Pathway two, has provided NSW Health with their full name, contact details, pharmacist registration number, intended services and location of services via the form at: https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/pharmaceutical/Pages/expanded-services-application.aspx' (page 5)

open_questions.topic: Dose, strength (for oral agents), frequency, quantity and treatment duration are not printed in this instrument
open_questions.observed: Clause 2 lists substances and some topical strengths but no dose, frequency, quantity or treatment duration. Clause 3(b) refers to 'the duration of treatment specified in the relevant Practice Standards'.
open_questions.why_unclear: The four NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards (impetigo, herpes zoster, atopic dermatitis, plaque psoriasis) are separate documents not included in this PDF. Nothing was inferred; treatment dose/frequency/duration fields are left blank.

open_questions.topic: Clause 2 substance list spans pages 1-2; the clause heading is printed only on page 1
open_questions.observed: '2) Restricted substances to which this instrument applies' is printed on page 1; the list continues onto page 2 (Flucloxacillin, Cefalexin, clause 2(b), 2(c), 2(d) entries) with no repeated heading before '3) Conditions — Limitation on supply' on the same page.
open_questions.why_unclear: Treatment rows on page 2 carry section_heading '2) Restricted substances to which this instrument applies' as the nearest heading above the content (continued from page 1); the heading itself is not reprinted on page 2.

open_questions.topic: Referral circumstances and age/other factor supply limitations are deferred to separate documents
open_questions.observed: Clause 3(d) incorporates 'any limitations on the supply of medicines indicated in clause 2 to a patient based on their age or other factor, and circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional' from the relevant Practice Standards.
open_questions.why_unclear: The specific trigger wording, thresholds, referral destinations and urgency levels are not printed in this instrument, so RF-1 and RF-2 are qualitative (structured: null) and the referral block lists only routine referral wording. Age triggers (RF-3 to RF-7) are structured from the clause 5 Definitions age bands, which ARE printed.

open_questions.topic: Two-column training tables garbled in text extraction (Training Pathway 1 and Training Pathway 2)
open_questions.observed: Training Pathway 1 renders as interleaved fragments ('Australasian College of Pharmaceutical Society of / Pharmacy education on OR Australia NSW education on / Dermatological Conditions; Dermatological Conditions;') and Training Pathway 2 as ('The Queensland / James Cook University's / University of Technology's / Prescribing / Extended community practice / Safe prescribing and OR / training pharmacists course (subject / quality use of / PC6300 only). / medicines course AND … PC6100 and PC6200 only').
open_questions.why_unclear: Row/column alignment cannot be reconstructed reliably from flat text. INC-9 summarises both pathways and the added requirement of 'Any additional training module(s) that have been approved by the Chief Health Officer and listed on the NSW Health website', but the exact cell-by-cell wording must be verified against the PDF.

open_questions.topic: Eligibility age bounds are indication-specific; eligibility.age_bounds records only the combined envelope
open_questions.observed: Clause 5 gives four different bands: atopic dermatitis 2-65 years (inclusive); herpes zoster 18 years or older; impetigo 2 years or older; psoriasis 18 years or older.
open_questions.why_unclear: The schema allows a single min/max pair, so min_years 2 / max_years 65 is the outer envelope only; the engine must apply the indication-specific band (INC-1 to INC-4 / EXC-2 to EXC-5 / RF-3 to RF-7), not the envelope alone.

open_questions.observed: '6) Commencement — This authority commences on publication.' The instrument is 'Dated: 28 August 2026' and the instrument it revokes was 'signed 29 August 2025'.
open_questions.why_unclear: The publication date (and therefore the exact effective date) is not stated in the document; effective_date records the date of the instrument plus this note.

open_questions.observed: Record-production and consent-sharing requirements are in clause 3(h) and 3(i) (page 3); the NSW Health expanded-services registration requirement for Training Pathway two pharmacists appears in clause 5 Definitions (page 5).
open_questions.why_unclear: A single provenance object covers the block at its first page (page 3); each condition carries its own inline page reference.

open_questions.topic: Inclusion criteria are grouped in two criteria_groups (document does not state combinatorics explicitly)
open_questions.observed: Clause 3 opens 'An approved pharmacist may supply the restricted substance listed in clause 2 to an applicable patient, subject to the conditions that:' (conjunctive conditions a-j), while clause 5 pairs each indication with its own age band.
open_questions.why_unclear: INC-1 to INC-4 are grouped as any_of (the indication-specific age/indication pair for the presentation), INC-5 to INC-11 as all_of (common conditions). The two groups combine by AND per the 'subject to the conditions that' wording; the document does not spell out AND/OR notation.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Obtain the four current 'relevant Practice Standards' (NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for management of impetigo; herpes zoster; acute exacerbations of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis; acute exacerbations of mild plaque psoriasis) and transcribe their treatment duration/quantity limits, age or other factor supply limitations, and referral circumstances.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Clause 3(b) and 3(d) incorporate these limits and referral triggers by reference; none are printed in this PDF, so eligibility/escalation rules for the four indications cannot be completed without them.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm which training pathway each local pharmacist completed: Training Pathway 1 (Australasian College of Pharmaceutical Society of Australia / NSW education on Dermatological Conditions PLUS any CHO-approved additional training module(s)) OR Training Pathway 2 (Queensland University of Technology Safe prescribing and quality use of medicines course subject PC6300, and/or James Cook University Extended community practice pharmacists course subjects PC6100 and PC6200, PLUS additional approved module(s)).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The training tables are two-column and interleaved in the text extraction; the exact pathway wording and AND/OR structure must be verified against the PDF before go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm whether each pharmacist completed Training Pathway two, which triggers the requirement to provide NSW Health with their full name, contact details, pharmacist registration number, intended services and location of services via https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/pharmaceutical/Pages/expanded-services-application.aspx.
